preferredPrimitives: m.* components (never motion.*) inside LazyMotion strict
patterns: git vocabulary as structure: commit header, releases, merged branches, side branches, open a PR

must: Use only real content from app/data/portfolio.ts and public/resume.pdf; never invent clients, numbers, testimonials or awards.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion; no WebGL, post-processing or heavy effects; Lighthouse mobile 90+ and accessibility 100.
Responsive 320–1920px without horizontal overflow; 44px minimum touch targets; visible focus.
Signal lime is only a background behind --on-signal text.
avoid: The SHIFENMEI identity (dark ink + cinnabar, 十, Mona Sans / Martian Mono / Instrument Serif).
Raster avatars or portraits of Hemal (removed at the owner's request).
Raster screenshots — project visuals are code-built mockups.
Container queries for mockup sizing (measured ~2x layout cost); use --mw.
Hiding the header on scroll — it must stay reachable.

decisions: Concept 'Merged to main': the portfolio is a git history. See docs/DESIGN.md.
Tea-estate paper palette with automatic dark theme; Bricolage Grotesque + JetBrains Mono.
Motion (lazy features) drives magnetic CTAs and odometers; lens, pinned stage, typing and cursor are small vanilla loops; scroll effects are CSS scroll-driven.
21st.dev-style components were written locally because 21st.dev is not reachable from the build environment.
Project visuals are code-built mockups; the code under the X-ray lens is illustrative and labelled so.
Effects adapted from the SHIFENMEI site (lens, pinned showcase, odometer, cursor, Lenis) in this portfolio's own identity.
A code-modelled cartoon guide bot (three.js, lazy) leads visitors through the sections; it is generic, not a likeness of the owner.

Afterhours is an original standalone cinematic city-guide concept inspired by the scroll-story format of Fly Crooked; free Pexels night photography, acid-lime/ink palette, Barlow Condensed typography, reduced-motion fallback and interactive route dialogs. It uses the established public/showcase integration.

Afterhours scroll was corrected to a single pinned film with scroll-driven camera zoom, overlapping scenes and timed text beats. Crunch Club adds an original playful food-brand concept with free Pexels imagery, ingredient interaction and a flavour builder.

Second rebuild: Afterhours uses an original alley texture on depth-shaped WebGL geometry, six timed story beats, a 3D-transformed phone route prototype, real asset readiness and smooth menu anchors. Crunch Club uses original transparent ingredient artwork recombined into an assembled sandwich, a five-beat pinned story and an exploded ingredient interaction. Both share a local Lenis runtime, loader fallback, modal scroll locking and reduced-motion behavior.

Owner rejected asterisk marks. Replace them with an original Afterhours doorway and Crunch Club bite outline. Use amber/ink for city wayfinding, masked headline reveals, a train-window chapter, accessible scene navigation and a photo-rich pinned food collage; retain all requested scroll animation.

After repeated visual feedback, replace the depth-only city surface with an original Three.js street: independent buildings, windows, balconies, cables, shops, road and skyline, projection-textured from the original environment artwork; real camera travel and an unobstructed vertical rise. Crunch Club shifts to Fredoka rounded display type, cut-paper outlines, diagonal sandwich art, oval photography and cream/sage story transitions.

Owner supplied six full-page Bánh Mì Vietnam references: add all missing editorial chapters to Crunch Club, including floating evolution photos, scroll-stacked dated history cards, a complete anatomy spread, inline-image fillings typography, a keyboard and touch photo carousel and a photo-backed torn-paper finale. Use original copy and identity with credited free Pexels photography; retain the opening sandwich animation and flavour builder.

Latest owner direction supersedes earlier city/food concepts: match reference palettes, typography, imagery and complete section sequences. Afterhours is a credited Crow / Fly Crooked motion study using its published illustrated film assets; Crunch Club is a credited HoQuan / Bánh Mì Vietnam editorial study using its imagery. Implement original scroll/render code with bounded city frame decoding, mobile layouts, reliable readiness and accessible reduced-motion chapters. Do not describe these studies as original commissioned designs or claim source awards.

Smoothness correction: Afterhours uses derived H.264 chapter films with frequent keyframes, browser video compositing and at most three retained decoders, replacing repeated network image fetching, bitmap eviction and canvas drawing. Crunch restores staged heading, ingredient and paper reveals with independent Web Animations transforms, updates history accessibility state only at boundaries, caches carousel measurements, removes redundant raster filters and promotes only active scroll layers. Shared Lenis uses frame-rate-independent interpolation for wheel input while retaining deliberate two-second chapter navigation.

Ceylon Select preview uses its real tea photographs and an independent paper/forest/gold identity. The owner requested richer loading and hero motion and fully visible products: use a brief leaf-drawing curtain intro, staggered masked serif headlines, composited product drift that pauses outside the hero, self-hosted fonts, and three contained product photographs in the closing scene. Preserve the compact arrow icons and reduced-motion fallback.
